# This Markdown file contains all the code to scrape data from Wyoming's k12 and higher education job postings

## Part 1: Wyoming K12 Data

### Loop K12 data from every district on a direct scraping platform
```{r loop with districts on a direct scraping platform, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(edjobs)
source("direct_api_scrapers.R")

# k12_district_registry.csv is the single source of truth for every K-12
# district scraped from a real structured platform (Applitrack, TedK12,
# SchoolSpring, RedRoverK12) -- District/Platform/Job_Link, plus Org_ID for
# RedRoverK12's numeric org ID (not derivable from its URL slug alone).
# Replaces three separate, independently-maintained link CSVs
# (Frontline_job_links.csv, tedk12_job_links.csv, springer_job_links.csv)
# that used to carry the SAME district under three different spellings in
# practice ("Converse County School Distrcit 2", "Albany Count School
# District 1", "Campbell County Scholl District 1") -- exactly the
# canonicalize_k12_district() misspellings this project has had to patch
# around downstream for months. One row per district here means one
# spelling to get right, checked by tests/testthat/test-drift-check.R's
# equivalent (registry-consistency is exercised via the pipeline's own
# equivalence tests, not a dedicated schema test since this project's
# existing convention is to test behavior, not file shape). A district
# migrating platforms in the future (several already have -- Butte-style
# moves aren't unique to Montana) is a one-row edit here, not a code change.
#
# fetch_applitrack_postings()/fetch_tedk12_postings()/
# fetch_schoolspring_postings()/fetch_redrover_postings() (all
# direct_api_scrapers.R) are unchanged from their original per-platform
# loops -- only the dispatch is unified. Each district is still logged
# individually via safe_scrape() so one district's outage (a few
# Applitrack tenants genuinely return HTTP 500 from Applitrack's own
# servers, independent of this scraper -- confirmed 2026-08-02) doesn't
# block the rest of the registry.
registry <- read.csv("k12_district_registry.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

all_direct_data <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(registry))) {
  row <- registry[i, ]

  district_jobs <- switch(row$Platform,
    Applitrack = {
      tenant_path <- applitrack_tenant_path(row$Job_Link)
      df <- safe_scrape(
        row$District,
        scrape_fn = function() fetch_applitrack_postings(tenant_path),
        expected_cols = c("title", "position", "position2", "date_posted", "location", "closing_date")
      )
      # A genuinely empty result is dropped, not padded with a placeholder
      # row -- matching every other platform in this same loop (TedK12/
      # SchoolSpring/RedRoverK12 below). The original Applitrack loop
      # inserted a literal title = "No jobs" row here instead, which
      # combinedclean.csv then carried straight into production as a fake
      # posting -- classified "Other", counted in that district's weekly
      # total, with no code anywhere filtering the literal string back out
      # (confirmed: 3 such rows in the 2026-08-28 committed
      # combinedclean.csv, for Fremont County SD24, Lincoln County SD1, and
      # Sublette County SD9). safe_scrape() already logs an empty week to
      # scrape_log.csv/drift_check.R same as it does for every other
      # platform, so this placeholder was never actually needed to make an
      # empty week visible.
      # Each posting's url is its own AppliTrack page and its posting_id
      # AppliTrack's job ID (applitrack_posting_url()), so postings sharing a
      # title stay apart; the board URL and fingerprint only without an ID.
      # Close_Date is the board's "Closing Date" as written.
      if (nrow(df) > 0) {
        df <- ensure_posted_pay_columns(df)
        job_id <- if ("job_id" %in% names(df)) df$job_id else rep(NA_character_, nrow(df))
        data.frame(title = df$title, date_posted = df$date_posted, position = df$position,
                   location = df$location,
                   url = dplyr::coalesce(applitrack_posting_url(tenant_path, job_id), row$Job_Link),
                   posting_id = ifelse(is.na(job_id), NA_character_, paste0("applitrack:", tenant_path, ":", job_id)),
                   District = row$District,
                   Close_Date = if ("closing_date" %in% names(df)) df$closing_date else NA_character_,
                   Pay_Min = df$Pay_Min, Pay_Max = df$Pay_Max, Pay_Unit = df$Pay_Unit,
                   Pay_Text = df$Pay_Text, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      } else {
        NULL
      }
    },
    TedK12 = {
      df <- safe_scrape(
        row$District,
        scrape_fn = function() fetch_tedk12_postings(row$Job_Link),
        expected_cols = c("title", "date_posted", "position", "location", "url")
      )
      if (nrow(df) > 0) {
        data.frame(title = df$title, date_posted = df$date_posted, position = df$position,
                   location = df$location, url = df$url, District = row$District,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      } else {
        NULL
      }
    },
    SchoolSpring = {
      domain_name <- schoolspring_domain(row$Job_Link)
      df <- safe_scrape(
        row$District,
        scrape_fn = function() fetch_schoolspring_postings(domain_name),
        expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Posting_ID", "Link")
      )
      if (nrow(df) > 0) {
        df$District <- row$District
        # Each posting's own record adds Close_Date (the deadline applicants
        # see; NA for "Posted until filled"), Job_Status (raw archive only)
        # and posted pay (add_schoolspring_details()). A failed detail
        # request leaves only that posting's fields NA.
        if ("Link" %in% names(df)) df <- add_schoolspring_details(df)
        out <- normalize_id_backed_k12_postings(df)
        out$Close_Date <- if ("Close_Date" %in% names(df)) df$Close_Date else NA_character_
        out$Job_Status <- if ("Job_Status" %in% names(df)) df$Job_Status else NA_character_
        out
      } else {
        NULL
      }
    },
    RedRoverK12 = {
      org_slug <- redrover_org_slug(row$Job_Link)
      df <- safe_scrape(
        row$District,
        scrape_fn = function() fetch_redrover_postings(as.character(row$Org_ID), org_slug),
        expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Posting_ID", "Link")
      )
      if (nrow(df) > 0) {
        df$District <- row$District
        normalize_id_backed_k12_postings(df)
      } else {
        NULL
      }
    },
    stop("Unknown Platform in k12_district_registry.csv: ", row$Platform)
  )

  if (!is.null(district_jobs) && nrow(district_jobs) > 0) {
    all_direct_data[[length(all_direct_data) + 1]] <- district_jobs
  }
}

direct_all <- bind_rows(all_direct_data)

# Save the extracted data to a CSV file
write.csv(direct_all, "all_direct_k12_job_listings.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

### Combine all the k12 data include a few manual pulls from unique district sites
#### Be sure to update your manually scraped data
#### This will populate your app folder for your Shiny application
```{r combine all the data into one dataframe, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(stringr)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)


standardize_date <- function(x) {

  # Convert factor to character safely
  x <- as.character(x)

  # Remove timezone text like "(UTC)"
  x <- str_remove(x, "\\s*\\(.*\\)$")

  # Parse known formats
  parsed <- parse_date_time(
    x,
    orders = c(
      "b d Y h:M p",   # Oct 23 2025 6:00 AM
      "B d Y h:M p",   # October 23 2025 6:00 AM
      "ymd",
      "mdy",
      "dmy",
      "Y-m-d H:M:S"
    ),
    tz = "UTC",
    quiet = TRUE
  )

  as.Date(parsed)
}



direct <- read.csv("all_direct_k12_job_listings.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# The 12 districts not on any major platform were previously hand-
# maintained in otherjobs.xlsx (no code in this repo ever wrote that
# file -- it was 5 months stale). Replaced with a real pipeline: WSBA's
# statewide vacancies page (clean structured data, but confirmed
# incomplete -- misses ~60-75% of real postings, systematically dropping
# classified/support/substitute/coaching roles) combined with each
# district's own page (heuristic per-platform extraction, deduplicated
# against that district's WSBA entries by normalized title). See
# misc_district_scrapers.R's header comment for the full platform
# breakdown and known limitations.
library(edjobs)
source("direct_api_scrapers.R")
source("misc_district_scrapers.R")

other <- safe_scrape(
  "Miscellaneous K-12 districts (WSBA + own pages)",
  scrape_fn = function() {
    fetch_all_misc_district_postings(
      chromote_session_factory = function() chromote::ChromoteSession$new()
    )
  },
  expected_cols = c("title", "date_posted", "position", "location", "url", "District")
)

# Laramie Montessori Charter School: not a school district at all (so it
# has no natural home in misc_district_registry, which is keyed by
# District), but was found to have its own clean structured source
# (Paylocity) while investigating Wyoming's charter schools -- see
# direct_api_scrapers.R::fetch_paylocity_jobs(). Snowy Range Academy, the
# other real charter school found, already surfaces via WSBA with no
# extra code needed since WSBA already treats it as a standalone org.
laramie_montessori <- safe_scrape(
  "Laramie Montessori Charter School",
  scrape_fn = function() fetch_paylocity_jobs("70f7d03b-6c9f-4106-8e70-9d781a8bbcba", "Laramie-Montessori-School-Inc"),
  expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Link")
)
if (nrow(laramie_montessori) > 0) {
  laramie_montessori <- data.frame(
    title = laramie_montessori$Title,
    date_posted = laramie_montessori$Posted_Date,
    position = NA_character_,
    location = laramie_montessori$Location,
    url = laramie_montessori$Link,
    District = "Laramie Montessori Charter School",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  other <- dplyr::bind_rows(other, laramie_montessori)
}

direct <- direct %>%
  mutate(date_posted = standardize_date(date_posted))

other <- other %>%
  mutate(date_posted = standardize_date(date_posted))

is_wsba <- other$District %in% registry$District | (!is.na(other$url) & other$url == WSBA_VACANCIES_URL)
wsba_rows <- remove_wsba_direct_duplicates(
  other[is_wsba, , drop = FALSE],
  direct,
  report_path = "wy_discrepancy_report.csv"
)
# WSBA keeps listing postings the district has closed (20 of 23 checked on
# 2026-11-05). Each kept WSBA row that links a district posting is checked on
# its platform, and the closed ones are dropped (posting_status.R). A failed
# check keeps the row; a failure of the whole step keeps them all.
library(edjobs)
wsba_checks <- tryCatch(
  check_posting_pages(wsba_rows$url, Sys.Date(), session_factory = function() chromote::ChromoteSession$new()),
  error = function(e) { message("WSBA posting checks skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
if (!is.null(wsba_checks) && nrow(wsba_checks) > 0) {
  n_before <- nrow(wsba_rows)
  wsba_rows <- drop_closed_wsba_rows(wsba_rows, wsba_checks)
  message(sprintf("WSBA posting checks: %d page(s) checked, %d closed WSBA row(s) dropped.",
                  nrow(wsba_checks), n_before - nrow(wsba_rows)))
  k <- match(wsba_checks$Check_URL, posting_status_check_url(other$url))
  wsba_checks$Segment <- "K-12"
  wsba_checks$District <- other$District[k]
  wsba_checks$Title <- other$title[k]
  wsba_checks$Last_Listed <- format(Sys.Date())
}
other_rows <- other[!is_wsba, , drop = FALSE]

combined <- dplyr::bind_rows(direct, other_rows, wsba_rows) %>%
  mutate(Archive_Date = Sys.Date())

# fix_title_encoding() (k12_he_classification.R) is applied here, once, at
# the point titles first enter the pipeline -- not just inside
# classify_k12_position()/classify_k12_subject() below, which only fixed a
# private copy used for regex matching and discarded it. Without this, a
# title with a raw Windows-1252 byte (an en dash in a time range, etc.) from
# any non-Applitrack source (TedK12/SchoolSpring/RedRover/misc-district) would
# classify correctly but still archive and display with the mangled byte,
# since the archived CSV below and combinedclean's `title` column both come
# from this same `combined` object. move_title_detail() then cuts detail a
# board put in the title (a requirement, the pay, "Open Until Filled", a
# file name) and fills Posted Pay from it where the row has none; before the
# posting_id, so the ID is built from the cleaned title.
combined <- combined %>%
  mutate(title = fix_title_encoding(title)) %>%
  move_title_detail() %>%
  mutate(
    posting_id = build_k12_posting_id(
      source_id = posting_id,
      title = title,
      location = location,
      date_posted = date_posted,
      url = url,
      district = canonicalize_k12_district(District)
    )
  )

file_name <- paste0("combined_", Sys.Date(), ".csv")

# Write the data to a CSV file with the new file name
write.csv(combined, file=file.path('Archivek12_Data',file_name), row.names = FALSE)

# How SchoolSpring postings that left the board ended (filled / canceled /
# review), from each posting's own record; posting-dates plan step 4. Reads
# the raw archives just written; a failure here never stops the run.
tryCatch(refresh_schoolspring_endings("Archivek12_Data", "schoolspring_endings.csv"),
         error = function(e) message("SchoolSpring endings not updated: ", conditionMessage(e)))

# BLS OEWS regional pay by role, the labeled fallback for postings that state
# no pay (bls_oews_scraper.R). Refreshed only when BLS publishes a new year;
# a failed check keeps the committed file. Counties come from last run's
# salarymap2.csv (district -> "Albany County, Wyoming").
library(edjobs)
oews_path <- file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "oews_role_wages.csv")
tryCatch(refresh_oews_wages("WY", oews_path),
         error = function(e) log_reference_result(oews_path, "error", conditionMessage(e)))

# BLS QCEW average pay of public school employees by county (all roles), the
# map popup's county context (qcew_school_pay.R). A failed fetch keeps the
# existing file, and so does a partial or implausible one (write_reference_file()).
library(edjobs)
qcew_path <- file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "qcew_county_school_pay.csv")
tryCatch(write_reference_file(fetch_qcew_school_pay("56"), qcew_path),
         error = function(e) log_reference_result(qcew_path, "error", conditionMessage(e)))
oews_wages <- read.csv(oews_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                       colClasses = c(Area_Code = "character", SOC = "character", Year = "character"))
district_county <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, c("District", "County")]

# Categorize positions in the "position" column of the "combinedclean" dataset.
# classify_k12_position() lives in k12_he_classification.R (sourced above) so
# this week's raw jobs-table classification and the accumulated-history
# append below can't silently drift apart.

# Drop byte-identical duplicate rows BEFORE classify_k12_position() below
# overwrites the raw `position` column. Some direct-platform pages (e.g.
# Sweetwater County SD1's Applitrack "?all=1" listing) render the same
# opening once per building it applies to and the modern scraper emits N
# identical rows for it -- build_k12_posting_id() already collapses those to
# one posting_id, but k12_district_weekly_totals below is a raw count() of
# rows, so the duplicates inflated a handful of districts' weekly totals
# (Sweetwater SD1: 96 rows for 80 real openings). This must happen on the
# raw row: older SchoolSpring snapshots carry the building name in `position`
# (distinguishing 26 genuinely separate "one coach per school" postings that
# share a title), and once classify_k12_position() replaces that with a
# bucket they would collapse wrongly. The distinct key is the full row,
# date_posted included -- two rows differing only by a re-dated date_posted
# may be a real re-posting, which the WSBA dedup step deliberately keeps too.
# rebuild_k12_history_from_archive() dedupes at the identical point so the
# from-archive rebuild stays equivalent (test-history-accumulator.R).
# Then (build_k12_combinedclean(), history_accumulator.R, shared with the
# from-archive rebuild): placeholder board entries ("Sample Certified
# Position", account-creation templates) are kept in the raw archive above but
# never counted as jobs; Pay_* is the pay the posting itself states
# (extract_posted_pay()), NA where the source states none or the amount is
# implausible for its unit (drop_implausible_pay(); the raw archive keeps it
# as scraped); Est_* is the BLS regional median for the posting's role,
# matched to its district's county (statewide where the county is unknown).
source("history_accumulator.R")
combinedclean <- combined %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  collapse_duplicate_posting_ids("combinedclean") %>%
  build_k12_combinedclean(oews_wages, district_county, "WY")

write.csv(combinedclean, file=file.path('Wy_Ed_Jobs','combinedclean.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

#--------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Append this week's newly classified rows onto the existing accumulated
# history, instead of reprocessing every archived raw snapshot from
# scratch every run -- see history_accumulator.R's header for why (100+
# archive files and growing, O(all history) work every week on a 30-minute
# CI budget). append_weekly_rows() is idempotent (a same-day re-run
# replaces, not duplicates, that day's rows) and asserts the new week's
# columns match the existing file's before writing anything.
#
# For disaster recovery, or to independently verify this incremental path
# hasn't drifted, scripts/rebuild_k12_history_from_archive.R rebuilds these
# same files from scratch from the raw archive -- that's also what
# tests/testthat/test-history-accumulator.R checks this incremental path
# against, using the real archived data in this repo.
#--------------------------------------------------------------------------
source("history_accumulator.R")

this_week_k12jobs <- build_k12_teacher_rows(combinedclean)

k12jobs <- append_weekly_rows(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "k12jobanalysis.csv"), this_week_k12jobs)
write.csv(k12jobs, file=file.path('Wy_Ed_Jobs','k12jobanalysis.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

# Per-district weekly posting totals (ALL categories, not just Teacher) --
# powers the sparkline trend shown next to each district's raw count on
# the landing page's "Top K-12 Hiring Districts" table. Built from the
# same combinedclean used above, just not filtered to position == "Teacher".
this_week_district_totals <- combinedclean %>%
  count(District, Archive_Date, name = "n")
k12_district_weekly_totals <- append_weekly_rows(
  file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "k12_district_weekly_totals.csv"), this_week_district_totals)
write.csv(k12_district_weekly_totals, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "k12_district_weekly_totals.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


#Database for all dates by category
# Dedup key is posting_id, not title+location: two real vacancies can have
# identical display text but distinct source IDs (as SchoolSpring does).
#
# The Total row is computed as the SUM of the per-district counts below, not
# as its own independent n_distinct() over every district's rows combined.
# Some scrapers fall back to a generic location placeholder (literally the
# string "District") when they can't extract a real school name, and two
# different districts can both produce that same generic title+location
# combination for two genuinely different real postings; deduping across
# district boundaries would silently collapse those into one and undercount
# the Total relative to its own parts.
#
# Both this week's Total and per-district rows are computed from
# this_week_k12jobs alone (one Archive_Date), not the full accumulated
# k12jobs -- the group_by already includes Archive_Date, so each week's
# counts are independent of every other week's, and only this week's
# slice needs to be computed fresh.
this_week_k12sumdistrict <- summarize_k12_posting_counts(this_week_k12jobs)

this_week_k12sum <- this_week_k12sumdistrict %>%
  group_by(Broad_Category, Archive_Date) %>%
  summarize(sum = sum(sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(District = "Total") %>%
  select(Broad_Category, Archive_Date, District, sum)

# Consistency check for the append logic itself, not the underlying data --
# this week's Total must equal the sum of this week's own district rows
# before either is ever written to the accumulated history. See
# history_accumulator.R::check_total_matches_parts().
check_total_matches_parts(this_week_k12sum, this_week_k12sumdistrict,
                           group_cols = c("Broad_Category", "Archive_Date"))

this_week_allsum <- bind_rows(this_week_k12sum, this_week_k12sumdistrict)
Allsum <- append_weekly_rows(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "allsum.csv"), this_week_allsum)
write.csv(Allsum, file=file.path('Wy_Ed_Jobs','allsum.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

# Database for all data NOW by category -- always just this week's
# snapshot, so unlike the datasets above this never needed the archive
# rebuild in the first place; it's built straight from this week's own
# district-level summary computed above.
k12districtnowsum <- this_week_k12sumdistrict %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(Sum = sum) %>%
  select(Broad_Category, Sum, District)

k12nowsum <- k12districtnowsum %>%
  group_by(Broad_Category) %>%
  summarize(Sum = sum(Sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(District = "Total")

Allnow <- bind_rows(k12nowsum, k12districtnowsum)

write.csv(Allnow, file=file.path('Wy_Ed_Jobs','allnow.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

list<-unique(this_week_k12jobs$District)
write.csv(list, "list.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### K-12 salary data, from WSBA's publicly shared PDFs
```{r wsba salary data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("salary_scrapers.R")

teacher_salary <- safe_scrape(
  "WSBA teacher salary settlements",
  scrape_fn = fetch_wsba_teacher_salary,
  expected_cols = c("District", "Base_Salary_Prior_Year", "Base_Salary_Current_Year", "Salary_Year")
)

superintendent_salary <- safe_scrape(
  "WSBA superintendent salaries",
  scrape_fn = fetch_wsba_superintendent_salary,
  expected_cols = c("District", "Superintendent_Salary", "Superintendent_Contract_Days")
)

# Only the WSBA salary figures get refreshed from WSBA each run.
# Other columns (geo/links, CCD staffing, Census, WDE salaries) are preserved.
# District is already canonical in the file on disk.
salarymap2 <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8")

if (nrow(teacher_salary) > 0 && nrow(superintendent_salary) > 0) {
  salarymap2 <- salarymap2 %>%
    select(-any_of(c("Teacher_Base_Salary", "Teacher_Base_Salary_Prior_Year", "Salary_Year",
                     "Superintendent_Salary", "Superintendent_Contract_Days", "Salary_Source"))) %>%
    left_join(teacher_salary, by = "District") %>%
    left_join(superintendent_salary, by = "District") %>%
    rename(Teacher_Base_Salary = Base_Salary_Current_Year,
           Teacher_Base_Salary_Prior_Year = Base_Salary_Prior_Year) %>%
    # No "last updated" timestamp -- this data only changes once a year
    # (WSBA republishes a new Salary_Year settlement document), so a date
    # stamped fresh on every weekly pipeline run would just mislead people
    # into thinking the dollar figures themselves refresh that often.
    # Salary_Year is the real freshness signal.
    mutate(Salary_Source = "WSBA (wsba-wy.org)")

  write.csv(salarymap2, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

  # Starts building a multi-year K-12 salary trend -- WSBA has no public
  # historical archive (unlike IPEDS, checked directly 2026-08-05), so
  # this only accumulates real history going forward, one snapshot per
  # new Salary_Year.
  archive_k12_salary_snapshot(salarymap2, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "k12_salary_history.csv"))
} else {
  message("WSBA salary fetch failed for one or both documents -- leaving salarymap2.csv untouched this run.")
}

# District-level data-completeness classification (misc_district_scrapers.R)
# -- refreshed unconditionally every run, not gated on the salary fetch
# above, since it's a static structural fact about which platform each
# district is scraped from, not something that can itself fail to fetch.
# Every district not in misc_district_coverage_tiers() is scraped from a
# genuine structured job-board platform, hence the coalesce to "Full".
source("misc_district_scrapers.R")
salarymap2 <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>%
  select(-any_of("Data_Coverage")) %>%
  left_join(misc_district_coverage_tiers(), by = "District") %>%
  mutate(Data_Coverage = coalesce(Data_Coverage, "Full"))
write.csv(salarymap2, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### K-12 teacher FTE (staff headcount), from NCES's Common Core of Data via the Urban Institute API
```{r ccd teacher fte data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("ccd_staff_scraper.R")

teacher_fte <- safe_scrape(
  "CCD district teacher FTE (WY)",
  scrape_fn = fetch_ccd_teacher_fte,
  expected_cols = c("District", "Teachers_Total_FTE", "Enrollment", "CCD_Year")
)

salarymap2 <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8")

if (nrow(teacher_fte) > 0) {
  # No "last updated" timestamp -- same reasoning as the WSBA/IPEDS salary
  # chunks. CCD_Year is the real freshness signal for this data.
  # Drop last run's copies first: since salarymap2.csv is now read back with
  # every column kept, joining without this emitted Teachers_Total_FTE.x/.y,
  # Enrollment.x/.y and CCD_Year.x/.y, which verify_schema.R rejects.
  salarymap2 <- salarymap2 %>%
    select(-any_of(c("Teachers_Total_FTE", "Enrollment", "CCD_Year", "CCD_Source"))) %>%
    left_join(teacher_fte, by = "District") %>%
    mutate(CCD_Source = "NCES Common Core of Data via Urban Institute Education Data Portal (educationdata.urban.org)")

  write.csv(salarymap2, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("CCD teacher FTE fetch failed -- leaving salarymap2.csv untouched this run.")
}

# Map rows that aren't regular CCD districts: charter schools (a charter
# inside a host district has no district record; the 3 state-authorized ones
# do, but report staff only at the school), Wyoming Boys School (a Department
# of Family Services school) and Northeast Wyoming BOCES (a regional service
# agency; its LEAID, staff summed over its schools). CCD ids for their staffing
# and free/reduced lunch share (2026-11-09). Kept here, not in salarymap2.csv,
# where a 12-digit id would round-trip as a number.
WY_SCHOOL_LEVEL_IDS <- c(
  "Snowy Range Academy" = "560073000216",               # Albany County SD 1 (Laramie)
  "Laramie Montessori Charter School" = "560073000542", # Albany County SD 1 (Laramie)
  "Cheyenne Classical Academy" = "568025700597",
  "Wyoming Classical Academy" = "568025800598",
  "Prairie View Community School" = "568025900599",
  "Wyoming Boys School" = "568025100538",
  "Northeast Wyoming BOCES" = "5680180"
)
# Rows with no Census poverty geography of their own whose students are local:
# their surrounding district's rate stands in. Not the BOCES or Wyoming Boys
# School, whose students come from many districts.
WY_SURROUNDING_POVERTY <- c("Snowy Range Academy", "Laramie Montessori Charter School", "Cheyenne Classical Academy",
                            "Wyoming Classical Academy", "Prairie View Community School",
                            "STRIDE Learning Center", "Sweetwater County Child Developmental Center")
salarymap2 <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
entity_ids <- setNames(as.list(as.character(salarymap2$NCES_LEAID)), salarymap2$District)
entity_ids[names(WY_SCHOOL_LEVEL_IDS)] <- as.list(WY_SCHOOL_LEVEL_IDS)
entity_ids <- entity_ids[!vapply(entity_ids, function(x) is.na(x) || x == "NA", logical(1))]

charter_staff <- safe_scrape(
  "CCD school-level staffing (WY charters, Boys School, BOCES)",
  scrape_fn = function() {
    r <- find_latest_ccd_directory_year()
    sch <- fetch_ccd_school_directory(56, r$year)
    out <- parse_ccd_school_staffing(sch, entity_ids[names(WY_SCHOOL_LEVEL_IDS)])
    out$CCD_Year <- rep(r$year, nrow(out))
    out
  },
  expected_cols = c("District", "Teachers_Total_FTE", "Enrollment", "CCD_Year")
)
if (nrow(charter_staff) > 0) {
  i <- match(charter_staff$District, salarymap2$District)
  ok <- !is.na(i) & !is.na(charter_staff$Teachers_Total_FTE)
  salarymap2$Teachers_Total_FTE[i[ok]] <- charter_staff$Teachers_Total_FTE[ok]
  salarymap2$Enrollment[i[ok]] <- charter_staff$Enrollment[ok]
  salarymap2$CCD_Year[i[ok]] <- charter_staff$CCD_Year[ok]
}

# Free/reduced-price lunch share beside SAIPE's child poverty rate
# (fetch_ccd_frl_share(), ccd_staff_scraper.R); each entity's newest
# reporting year, kept from last run when the fetch fails.
frl <- safe_scrape(
  "CCD free/reduced-price lunch share (WY)",
  scrape_fn = function() fetch_ccd_frl_share(56, entity_ids),
  expected_cols = c("District", "Free_Reduced_Lunch_Share", "FRL_Schools_Reporting", "FRL_Year")
)
if (nrow(frl) > 0) {
  salarymap2 <- salarymap2 %>%
    select(-any_of(c("Free_Reduced_Lunch_Share", "FRL_Schools_Reporting", "FRL_Year"))) %>%
    left_join(frl, by = "District", relationship = "many-to-one")
}
write.csv(salarymap2, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### County-level context (income, rent, mining/energy employment share, population trend), from the Census Bureau's ACS 5-Year Estimates
```{r census county context data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("census_acs_scraper.R")

# CENSUS_API_KEY must be set (a GitHub Actions secret in CI, .Renviron
# locally) -- see census_acs_scraper.R's header for why this can't run
# without one. safe_scrape() catches a missing/invalid key the same way it
# catches any other fetch failure: logs it, leaves salarymap2.csv
# untouched this run, rather than crashing the whole pipeline.
county_context <- safe_scrape(
  "Census ACS county context (WY)",
  scrape_fn = fetch_census_county_context,
  expected_cols = c("County", "Median_Household_Income", "Median_Gross_Rent",
                     "Population", "ACS_Year", "Mining_Employment_Share", "Population_Change_Pct")
)

if (nrow(county_context) > 0) {
  # Joins on County, not District -- one County value maps to multiple
  # sibling districts (e.g. Sheridan County SD1 and SD2 both correctly
  # get the same Sheridan County figures), same one-to-many relationship
  # WSBA's own District-level salary data doesn't have but this genuinely
  # does. No "last updated" timestamp, same reasoning as the WSBA/CCD/
  # IPEDS chunks above -- ACS_Year is the real freshness signal, and this
  # is 5-year-smoothed data that doesn't meaningfully change week to week.
  # select(-any_of(...)) drops last run's copy of these columns first so
  # a re-run doesn't produce Median_Household_Income.x/.y duplicates --
  # only reached on a successful fetch, so a failed run leaves the
  # existing columns (and every other column) fully untouched, same as
  # every other salary/staffing chunk in this pipeline.
  salarymap2 <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>%
    select(-any_of(c("Median_Household_Income", "Median_Gross_Rent", "Population",
                      "ACS_Year", "Mining_Employment_Share", "Population_Change_Pct"))) %>%
    left_join(county_context, by = "County")
  write.csv(salarymap2, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("Census ACS county context fetch failed -- leaving salarymap2.csv untouched this run.")
}
```

### District-level child poverty rate, from the Census Bureau's SAIPE program
```{r census saipe child poverty data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("census_acs_scraper.R")  # census_saipe_scraper.R reuses census_api_key()/clean_acs_value()/WY_STATE_FIPS from here
source("census_saipe_scraper.R")

child_poverty <- safe_scrape(
  "Census SAIPE district child poverty rate (WY)",
  scrape_fn = fetch_census_saipe_child_poverty,
  expected_cols = c("District", "Child_Poverty_Rate", "SAIPE_Year")
)

if (nrow(child_poverty) > 0) {
  # Joins on District, not County -- real district-level data (the closest
  # free proxy to free/reduced-lunch eligibility at the actual district a
  # posting is in), unlike the county-context chunk above. Fremont County
  # School District 38 comes from SAIPE's elementary geography
  # (fetch_census_saipe_child_poverty()).
  prev_poverty <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
  salarymap2 <- prev_poverty %>%
    select(-any_of(c("Child_Poverty_Rate", "SAIPE_Year", "Child_Poverty_Basis"))) %>%
    left_join(child_poverty, by = "District", relationship = "many-to-one")
  # A charter or early-childhood center has no SAIPE geography of its own: the
  # district(s) it sits in stand in (surrounding_district_poverty(),
  # ccd_staff_scraper.R; a split town's rates averaged), named in
  # Child_Poverty_Basis so the dashboard says "surrounding district". A
  # geocoder failure keeps last run's value and is logged (2026-11-09 review).
  salarymap2$Child_Poverty_Basis <- NA_character_
  district_rates <- data.frame(LEAID = as.character(salarymap2$NCES_LEAID), Child_Poverty_Rate = salarymap2$Child_Poverty_Rate,
                               SAIPE_Year = salarymap2$SAIPE_Year, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  district_rates <- district_rates[!is.na(district_rates$LEAID) & district_rates$LEAID != "NA", , drop = FALSE]
  district_names <- setNames(salarymap2$District, as.character(salarymap2$NCES_LEAID))
  geo_failed <- character(0)
  for (i in which(salarymap2$District %in% WY_SURROUNDING_POVERTY & is.na(salarymap2$Child_Poverty_Rate))) {
    p <- surrounding_district_poverty(salarymap2$Latitude[i], salarymap2$Longitude[i], district_rates, district_names)
    if (p$status == "ok") {
      salarymap2$Child_Poverty_Rate[i] <- p$rate
      salarymap2$SAIPE_Year[i] <- p$year
      salarymap2$Child_Poverty_Basis[i] <- p$basis
    } else if (p$status == "failed") {
      geo_failed <- c(geo_failed, salarymap2$District[i])
      k <- match(salarymap2$District[i], prev_poverty$District)
      for (col in intersect(c("Child_Poverty_Rate", "SAIPE_Year", "Child_Poverty_Basis"), names(prev_poverty))) {
        if (!is.na(k)) salarymap2[[col]][i] <- prev_poverty[[col]][k]
      }
    }
  }
  log_scrape_result("Census geocoder (surrounding-district poverty, WY)",
                    status = if (length(geo_failed)) "error" else "ok",
                    n_rows = sum(!is.na(salarymap2$Child_Poverty_Basis)),
                    error_message = if (length(geo_failed)) paste("geocoder failed for:", paste(geo_failed, collapse = "; ")) else NA_character_)
  write.csv(salarymap2, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("Census SAIPE child poverty fetch failed -- leaving salarymap2.csv untouched this run.")
}
```

### Combine all the Higher Education data
#### This will populate your app folder for your Shiny application
```{r munge he data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(writexl)
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)

# Combine all datasets. Pay_* is the pay the posting states: the NEOGOV
# colleges (LCCC, Casper, Central, Gillette), the PeopleAdmin ones (Western,
# Eastern, Sheridan, Northwest) and UW carry it (NA where a posting states
# none). It's kept in hedata.xlsx and the raw archive, but not in the
# accumulated facultydata.csv below.
hedata <- list(lccc, casper, western, central, eastern, gillette, sheridan, northwest, UW) %>%
  lapply(function(df) {
    # bind_rows() won't mix a Date Posted_Date with a character one.
    df$Posted_Date <- as.character(df$Posted_Date)
    # Close_Date: PeopleAdmin's own close date (or "Open Until Filled");
    # NA for the other colleges.
    df$Close_Date <- if ("Close_Date" %in% names(df)) as.character(df$Close_Date) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(df))
    ensure_posted_pay_columns(df)
  }) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  select(Title, Location, Posted_Date, Institution, Link, Close_Date, all_of(POSTED_PAY_COLUMNS))

hedata$Posted_Date<- as.character(hedata$Posted_Date)

hedata <- hedata %>%
  mutate(Archive_Date = Sys.Date())

# Save data with a time stamp
file_name <- paste0("hedata_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx")

write_xlsx(hedata, path = file_name)

write_xlsx(hedata, path = file.path("Archived_HE_Data", file_name))

# Posting status (posting_status.R): every posting with a checkable page that
# dropped off its board since the last run (K-12 and higher ed), plus this
# run's WSBA checks, recorded in posting_status.csv: whether the platform says
# it closed, and the closing date it states. A failure here never stops the run.
tryCatch(refresh_posting_status("Archivek12_Data", "Archived_HE_Data", "posting_status.csv",
                                extra_checks = wsba_checks,
                                session_factory = function() chromote::ChromoteSession$new()),
         error = function(e) message("Posting status not updated: ", conditionMessage(e)))

# Coverage calendar (posting-dates plan step 2): every source's outcome this
# run (ok / empty / error / not_logged), so a posting that stops appearing is
# read as ended only when its source was healthy. Every source has been
# scraped by now; a failure here never stops the run. Employers seen only on
# WSBA's statewide page (BOCES, academies) take the WSBA feed's row.
library(edjobs)
tryCatch(refresh_coverage_calendar(
  "coverage_calendar.csv", "scrape_log.csv",
  k12_entities = read.csv("k12_district_registry.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)$District,
  data_k12 = unique(combined$District), data_he = unique(hedata$Institution),
  feeds = c("WSBA statewide feed" = "^WSBA statewide vacancies$",
            "WSBA + own-page districts (group)" = "^Miscellaneous K-12 districts")),
  error = function(e) message("Coverage calendar not updated: ", conditionMessage(e)))
# Non-postings (a scraped "Job Title" header, "No Jobs" notices) stay in the
# raw archive above but are dropped from everything shown or counted.
# Implausible posted pay is blanked the same way (drop_implausible_pay()).
hedata <- hedata %>% filter(!is_placeholder_posting(Title)) %>% drop_implausible_pay()
# Est_* is the institution's IPEDS average for the posting's staff category
# (ipeds_staff_salaries.csv from the previous run), the labeled fallback for
# staff postings that state no pay. Added after the raw archive write, so
# the archive stays as scraped.
source("ipeds_staff_salaries.R")
staff_path <- file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "ipeds_staff_salaries.csv")
if (file.exists(staff_path)) {
  he_unitids <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"))[, c("Name", "IPEDS_UNITID")]
  hedata <- attach_ipeds_staff_estimates(hedata, read.csv(staff_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                                                          colClasses = c(Year = "character")),
                                         he_unitids$IPEDS_UNITID[match(canonicalize_he_institution(hedata$Institution), he_unitids$Name)])
}
# University of Wyoming staff postings use UW's own salary book instead
# (uw_salary_book.R): the median salary of UW staff with the same title.
source("uw_salary_book.R")
uw_book_path <- file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "uw_salary_book.csv")
if (file.exists(uw_book_path) && "Est_Pay" %in% names(hedata)) {
  hedata <- attach_uw_salary_book_estimates(hedata, read.csv(uw_book_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}
write_xlsx(hedata, path = file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "hedata.xlsx"))

# Fix historical institution-name typos before anything downstream keys off
# Institution, so a college's history doesn't silently split across two
# spellings (see canonicalize_he_institution() in k12_he_classification.R).
# Applied to this week's raw hedata AFTER the xlsx archive writes above, so
# the archived raw snapshot keeps whatever spelling the scraper actually
# produced that week (the historical record of what really happened),
# while everything derived from here on uses the canonical name.
hedata <- hedata %>%
  mutate(Institution = canonicalize_he_institution(Institution))

# Job_Type/Category classification lives in k12_he_classification.R (sourced
# in setup). Adjunct/pooled titles get their own Job_Type, separate from
# "Instructor/Teacher/Faculty", so a standing adjunct-pool posting isn't
# counted the same as full-time faculty hiring.
this_week_he_cat <- hedata %>%
  mutate(Job_Type = classify_he_job_type(Title))

# Pay_*, Est_* and Close_Date are left out of facultydata.csv: its accumulated history predates
# pay capture, and append_weekly_rows() refuses a changed column set.
this_week_facultydata <- this_week_he_cat %>%
  filter(Job_Type %in% c("Instructor/Teacher/Faculty", "Adjunct/Part-Time Faculty")) %>%
  mutate(Category = classify_he_faculty_category(Title)) %>%
  select(-all_of(POSTED_PAY_COLUMNS), -any_of(c("Est_Pay", "Est_Pay_Unit", "Est_Occupation", "Est_Area", "Est_Year", "Est_Source", "Close_Date")))

#--------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Append this week's newly classified rows onto the existing accumulated
# history, instead of reprocessing every archived raw xlsx snapshot from
# scratch every run. See history_accumulator.R's header (also sourced in
# the K-12 chunk above -- sourcing again here is a cheap no-op) and
# scripts/rebuild_he_history_from_archive.R for the disaster-recovery /
# verification path.
#--------------------------------------------------------------------------
source("history_accumulator.R")

facultydata <- append_weekly_rows(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "facultydata.csv"), as.data.frame(this_week_facultydata))
# Also shipped to the repo root (gitignored/local-only) mirroring the
# Wy_Ed_Jobs/ copy, same as before.
write.csv(facultydata, "facultydata.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(facultydata, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "facultydata.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Per-institution weekly posting totals (ALL categories/job types, not
# just full-time faculty) -- powers the sparkline trend shown next to
# each institution's raw count on the landing page's "Top Higher Ed
# Hiring Institutions" table. Built from this week's hedata (already
# canonicalized above) before the Job_Type/faculty-only filter.
this_week_he_totals <- hedata %>%
  count(Institution, Archive_Date, name = "n")
he_institution_weekly_totals <- append_weekly_rows(
  file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "he_institution_weekly_totals.csv"), this_week_he_totals)
write.csv(he_institution_weekly_totals, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "he_institution_weekly_totals.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# facultydata includes both full-time-ish and Adjunct/Part-Time faculty
# (Job_Type column distinguishes them) so the "Current Faculty Trends"
# chart can show a full-time/part-time stacked breakdown; the Longitudinal
# Trends and New This Week views filter back down to Job_Type ==
# "Instructor/Teacher/Faculty" in app.R to keep their existing, unchanged
# meaning ("faculty hiring", not incl. the standing adjunct pool).
#
# Both this week's Total and per-institution rows are computed from
# this_week_facultydata alone (one Archive_Date) -- same reasoning as the
# K-12 allsum block above.
this_week_hesum <- this_week_facultydata %>%
  group_by(Category, Archive_Date, Job_Type) %>%
  summarize(sum = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Institution = "Total") %>%
  select(Category, Archive_Date, Institution, Job_Type, sum)

this_week_hesuminst <- this_week_facultydata %>%
  group_by(Category, Archive_Date, Institution, Job_Type) %>%
  summarise(sum = n(), .groups = "drop")

check_total_matches_parts(this_week_hesum, this_week_hesuminst,
                           group_cols = c("Category", "Archive_Date", "Job_Type"))

this_week_allsum_he <- bind_rows(this_week_hesum, this_week_hesuminst)
Allsum_he <- append_weekly_rows(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "allsum_he.csv"), this_week_allsum_he)
write.csv(Allsum_he, file = file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "allsum_he.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Database for all data NOW by category -- always just this week's
# snapshot, built straight from this_week_facultydata (no history needed).
henowsum <- this_week_hesum %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(Sum = sum) %>%
  select(Category, Job_Type, Sum, Institution)

henowinstsum <- this_week_facultydata %>%
  group_by(Category, Institution, Job_Type) %>%
  summarize(Sum = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  select(Category, Sum, Institution, Job_Type)

Allnow_he <- rbind(henowsum, henowinstsum)

write.csv(Allnow_he, file = file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "allnow_he.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### Higher Ed faculty salary data, from IPEDS via the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal API
```{r ipeds he salary data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("ipeds_salary_scraper.R")

he_salary <- safe_scrape(
  "IPEDS instructional staff salaries (WY)",
  scrape_fn = fetch_ipeds_he_salaries,
  expected_cols = c("Name", "Faculty_Avg_Salary", "Faculty_Avg_Salary_Professor",
                     "Faculty_Count", "Salary_Year", "Salary_Note")
)

# IPEDS non-instructional staff pay by category (ipeds_staff_salaries.R), the
# labeled fallback for HE staff postings that state no pay. The HE munge
# step reads it on the next run; a failed fetch keeps the existing file.
source("ipeds_staff_salaries.R")
local({
  unitids <- na.omit(read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"))$IPEDS_UNITID)
  staff_path <- file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "ipeds_staff_salaries.csv")
  tryCatch(write_reference_file(fetch_ipeds_staff_salaries(56, unitids), staff_path),
           error = function(e) log_reference_result(staff_path, "error", conditionMessage(e)))
})

# University of Wyoming salary book (uw_salary_book.R), read by the HE munge
# step on the next run. Downloaded only when UW links a new book; a failed
# check keeps the committed file.
source("uw_salary_book.R")
uw_book_path <- file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "uw_salary_book.csv")
tryCatch(refresh_uw_salary_book(uw_book_path),
         error = function(e) log_reference_result(uw_book_path, "error", conditionMessage(e)))

# Static geo/link fields (Longitude, Latitude, Link, County) stay hand-
# maintained -- only the salary figures get refreshed from IPEDS each run.
# County (added 2026-08-06) is the join key the census county context
# chunk below needs; kept here in this early select() so it survives
# untouched through this chunk the same way Longitude/Latitude/Link do.
# IPEDS_UNITID is carried through every select() in this chunk: it isn't
# re-fetched each run, and dropping it here once broke the weekly run (the HE
# spells generator joins on it).
salarymap <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>%
  select(Name, any_of("IPEDS_UNITID"), Longitude, Latitude, Link, County)

if (nrow(he_salary) > 0) {
  # No "last updated" timestamp -- same reasoning as the WSBA chunk above.
  # IPEDS reports this annually (Salary_Year is the real freshness signal),
  # so stamping today's date every weekly run would misrepresent how often
  # the actual dollar figures change.
  salarymap <- salarymap %>%
    left_join(he_salary, by = "Name") %>%
    mutate(Salary_Source = "IPEDS via Urban Institute Education Data Portal (educationdata.urban.org)")

  # Multi-year salary trend (current + 2 prior years) -- IPEDS is
  # queryable by year indefinitely, unlike WSBA (no public historical
  # archive; checked directly 2026-08-05). Pivoted to generic "N years
  # ago" column names, not literal year numbers, so the schema stays
  # stable as the calendar year rolls over -- app.R derives the real
  # year labels from Salary_Year - 1, Salary_Year - 2.
  salary_trend <- safe_scrape(
    "IPEDS instructional staff salary 3-year trend (WY)",
    scrape_fn = function() fetch_ipeds_he_salary_trend(n_years = 3),
    expected_cols = c("Name", "Year", "Faculty_Avg_Salary")
  )
  if (nrow(salary_trend) > 0) {
    latest_year <- max(salary_trend$Year)
    salary_trend_wide <- salary_trend %>%
      mutate(YearsAgo = latest_year - Year) %>%
      filter(YearsAgo > 0) %>%
      select(Name, YearsAgo, Faculty_Avg_Salary) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = YearsAgo, values_from = Faculty_Avg_Salary,
                          names_glue = "Faculty_Avg_Salary_Y{YearsAgo}Ago")
    salarymap <- salarymap %>% left_join(salary_trend_wide, by = "Name")
  }

  salarymap <- salarymap %>%
    select(Name, any_of("IPEDS_UNITID"), Longitude, Latitude, Link, County, Faculty_Avg_Salary, Faculty_Avg_Salary_Professor,
           Faculty_Count, Salary_Year, Salary_Note, Salary_Source,
           starts_with("Faculty_Avg_Salary_Y"))

  write.csv(salarymap, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("IPEDS salary fetch failed -- leaving salarymap.csv untouched this run.")
}
```

### Higher ed institution fall enrollment (FTE), from IPEDS via the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal API
```{r ipeds he enrollment data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("ipeds_salary_scraper.R")  # ipeds_enrollment_scraper.R reuses fetch_ipeds_paginated()/IPEDS_UNITID_MAP from here
source("ipeds_enrollment_scraper.R")

he_enrollment <- safe_scrape(
  "IPEDS fall enrollment FTE (WY)",
  scrape_fn = fetch_ipeds_he_enrollment,
  expected_cols = c("Name", "Enrollment", "Enrollment_Year")
)

# 5-year enrollment trend -- HE's analogue of the Census county context
# chunk's Population_Change_Pct, just at the institution level. A second,
# independent safe_scrape() call (like teacher_salary/superintendent_
# salary in the WSBA chunk above) rather than folded into
# fetch_ipeds_he_enrollment() itself, so a trend-fetch failure (a missing
# 5-years-back vintage) doesn't also block this week's current Enrollment
# figure from updating.
he_enrollment_trend <- safe_scrape(
  "IPEDS fall enrollment 5-year trend (WY)",
  scrape_fn = fetch_ipeds_he_enrollment_trend,
  expected_cols = c("Name", "Enrollment_Change_Pct")
)

if (nrow(he_enrollment) > 0) {
  # No "last updated" timestamp -- same reasoning as every other salary/
  # staffing chunk. Enrollment_Year is the real freshness signal, matching
  # salarymap2.csv's CCD_Year for the equivalent K-12 figure.
  #
  # Students_Per_Teacher is NOT stored here -- it's computed on the fly in
  # app.R's map_he (Enrollment / Faculty_Count), the same way map_k12
  # already computes it from Enrollment / Teachers_Total_FTE rather than
  # storing a derived ratio in salarymap2.csv.
  salarymap <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>%
    select(-any_of(c("Enrollment", "Enrollment_Year"))) %>%
    left_join(he_enrollment, by = "Name")
  write.csv(salarymap, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("IPEDS fall enrollment fetch failed -- leaving salarymap.csv untouched this run.")
}

# Written as its own read-modify-write against the just-updated file above
# (not folded into the same conditional block) so a trend-fetch failure
# alone can't blank out last week's good Enrollment_Change_Pct values --
# same "leave it alone, don't blank it out" behavior every other salary/
# staffing chunk in this pipeline already has on a failed fetch.
if (nrow(he_enrollment_trend) > 0) {
  salarymap <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>%
    select(-any_of("Enrollment_Change_Pct")) %>%
    left_join(he_enrollment_trend, by = "Name")
  write.csv(salarymap, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("IPEDS fall enrollment trend fetch failed -- leaving salarymap.csv's Enrollment_Change_Pct untouched this run.")
}
```

### Higher ed institution Pell Grant recipient share, from the US Dept. of Education's Federal Student Aid office via the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal API
```{r fsa he pell share data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)

}
```

### Higher ed institution county-level context (income, rent, mining/energy employment share, population trend), from the Census Bureau's ACS 5-Year Estimates
```{r census county context data he, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("census_acs_scraper.R")

# Reuses the exact same fetch_census_county_context() pipeline as the K-12
# chunk earlier in this file -- salarymap.csv's County column (hand-
# maintained the same way Latitude/Longitude already are, added
# 2026-08-06 -- each of Wyoming's 9 public HE institutions is a single
# campus with one real home county) was the only thing missing to make
# this join possible; no new scraper needed. Fetched independently rather
# than reusing the K-12 chunk's `county_context` variable, matching every
# other chunk in this file being self-contained and re-runnable on its
# own -- this data changes at most once a year, so a second cheap fetch
# costs nothing.
county_context_he <- safe_scrape(
  "Census ACS county context for HE institutions (WY)",
  scrape_fn = fetch_census_county_context,
  expected_cols = c("County", "Median_Household_Income", "Median_Gross_Rent",
                     "Population", "ACS_Year", "Mining_Employment_Share", "Population_Change_Pct")
)

if (nrow(county_context_he) > 0) {
  # select(-any_of(...)) drops last run's copy first so a re-run doesn't
  # produce .x/.y duplicates, only reached on a successful fetch -- same
  # "never blank out last week's good values on a failed fetch" pattern
  # the K-12 census chunk uses.
  salarymap <- read.csv(file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>%
    select(-any_of(c("Median_Household_Income", "Median_Gross_Rent", "Population",
                      "ACS_Year", "Mining_Employment_Share", "Population_Change_Pct"))) %>%
    left_join(county_context_he, by = "County")
  write.csv(salarymap, file.path("Wy_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("Census ACS county context fetch failed -- leaving salarymap.csv untouched this run.")
}
```
